headline: High: xonsh can read/write the filesystem and run shell commands, so pairing it with ComfyUI creates default-path data, command, and workflow-conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI has no clipboard/stdin channel and no MCP, so direct prompt injection into xonsh is not documented. However, xonsh can read filesystem contents and execute shell commands, while ComfyUI exposes files/workflows; if users manually bridge outputs through files, injected instructions could be carried across. The pathway is possible but not default.
conditions: IF the operator copies ComfyUI-generated text or metadata into files that xonsh later reads as commands
IF a shared workspace is used to shuttle prompts between ComfyUI and xonsh
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs in a separate directory from any shell scripts
Review any text copied from generated artifacts before pasting into xonsh
Use read-only handoff files for model outputs
Disable ad hoc copy-paste between the two tools during sensitive tasks

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, workflows, seeds, and model artifacts, while xonsh can read filesystem contents and has broad network egress. If they share a workspace, xonsh can access ComfyUI artifacts and potentially transmit them outward. This is a default-path leakage risk once both operate on the same files, even though ComfyUI itself is offline-capable.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are stored in a directory that xonsh can read
IF xonsh commands upload or print those artifacts to remote services
mitigations: Store ComfyUI artifacts in a directory xonsh cannot access
Run xonsh with network disabled for sensitive jobs
Separate credentials and environment variables from the shared workspace
Audit shell history for accidental file exfiltration commands

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI writes model/workflow files and xonsh can write arbitrary filesystem contents, so both agents can contend over the same directories. ComfyUI is asynchronous and xonsh can spawn subprocesses, which increases the chance of concurrent edits or partial writes. No locking mechanism is documented here, so the overlap is real in default shared-workspace use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project or model directory
IF xonsh scripts modify files while ComfyUI is loading or saving workflows
mitigations: Assign separate output directories to each agent
Pause xonsh writes while ComfyUI is saving artifacts
Use timestamped filenames to avoid collisions
Add a quick manual check for partially written files before reuse

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI can generate workflows, images, and metadata that xonsh may consume from stdin/stdout or files, and xonsh can then execute shell commands based on that input. Because xonsh has shell execution authority, treating ComfyUI output as authoritative can cascade into incorrect or unsafe actions. The pair lacks a documented verification step, so the risk is more than low.
conditions: IF xonsh scripts parse ComfyUI-produced text or workflow files without validation
IF downstream shell commands are generated from ComfyUI output
mitigations: Insert a manual review step before any shell action derived from ComfyUI output
Restrict xonsh scripts to allowlisted commands only
Validate workflow files against a schema before use
Log and diff generated artifacts before execution

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not request secrets or special residency-sensitive scopes, so there is no direct evidence of a regulatory mismatch. The only plausible compliance issue is operational logging or retention of shared artifacts, which is not documented as a default breach. I therefore keep this low and cite both profiles to show the absence of stronger compliance signals.
conditions: IF the operator stores regulated data in ComfyUI artifacts that xonsh logs or exports
IF a deployment policy requires residency controls not enforced by the shared workspace
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared artifacts
Turn off verbose shell logging for sensitive sessions
Keep compliance-sensitive jobs in a separate workspace
Document retention rules for generated files
